We select a metallic sphere and right square pyramid to demonstrate the external cloaking function of arbitrary object. As a proof of concept, we utilize genetic algorithm to obtain the optimal phase distributions. Simulation results verify that the deliberate metasurface is capable of hiding any irregular objects.

articleTitle: Characterisation of bulk semiconductor solar cell without antireflection coating
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this experiment, we investigated Bulk GaAs semiconductor solar cell without antireflection coating. This report shows I-V curves for light and no light conditions and the photoluminescence. From the diagrams, we can easily get open circuit voltage, short circuit current and photocurrent in a certain wavelength range. After calculating fill factor, maximum output power and band gap width was obtained. We further investigated the influence of these parameters to solar cell efficiency to inform methods of improving efficiency. We briefly highlight problems in manufacturing and possible future solutions.

articleTitle: Table of Contents
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Presents the table of contents/splash page of the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Technical Program
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Provides a schedule of conference events and a listing of which papers were presented in each session.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-band Base Station Antenna with Parasitic Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A dual band antenna with parasitic structure named as antenna on antenna (AoA) is proposed for fifth generation mobile communication system (5G). The proposed AoA consists of a low frequency dipole antenna and high frequency patch antenna arrays, which covers traditional LTE and 5G millimeter wave band. In order to reduce the size of base station antenna, the millimeter wave patch antenna arrays are parasitic on the low-frequency dipole. While the radiator of the low frequency antenna is utilized as the ground of the millimeter wave patch antenna arrays, both of the low frequency and high frequency antennas share the same dielectric substrate. The simulation results show that the impedance bandwidths of the AoA are 44% and 10.7% for the LTE and 5G bands respectively.

articleTitle: Improved High Gain Miniaturized Bow-Tie Antenna with AMC
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: An improved low frequency slotted bow-tie antenna and a novel artificial magnetic conductor reflector were proposed. The antenna metal patch is slotted to reduce the antenna working frequency band without enlarging the size. The artificial magnetic conductor reflects electromagnetic wave on its surface in-phase in specific frequency band. The reflector is designed for improving the gain of antenna by reflecting the wave in-phase. The slotted bow-tie antenna loaded with artificial magnetic conductor reflector works between 566 MHz to 1.177 GHz. Its gain is increased by 5 dB and its front-to-back ratio is 12-16 dB at from 500 MHz to 900 MHz frequency band. The antenna system is suitable for the application of ground penetrating radar.

articleTitle: Ocean Waves Inversion Based on Airborne Radar Images with Small Incident Angle
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The interferometric radar imaging altimeter is one of the main payloads of the "Guanlan" ocean science satellite proposed by the National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology of China. To evaluate the accuracy of the interferometric radar imaging altimeter in retrieving the ocean dynamic parameters, such as sea surface height (SSH), significant wave height (SWH), an airborne interferometric radar imaging altimeter experiment was carried out at Qingdao Xiaomaidao (XMD) sea area on March 31, 2019. In the research work of this paper, SSH and SWH have been retrieved based on the interferograms acquired by the airborne interferometric radar imaging altimeter. The comparisons of the retrieved SWH with the buoy measurements, and the results demonstrate that the difference is small. In addition, the retrieved results also demonstrate that the incident angle error is an important factor affects the accuracy of the retrieved SSH. When the incident angle error is 1°, it can cause a relative error of about 40% at the near range. Through this study, it can be concluded that the interferometric radar imaging altimeter images of "Guanlan" satellite in future can effectively retrieve some ocean wave information.

articleTitle: SERS Prediction with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) has become a spectroscopic detection technique widely used in many fields. This paper proposes a SERS electric field distribution prediction model based on deep learning, the average relative norm error of the test set is 3.6%. It takes about 3 minutes to perform an FDTD simulation for an Au nanosphere dimer on a high-performance server, while using the deep learning model on an ordinary PC only takes less than 0.003 seconds, which can be used as a kind of fast calculation tool in the optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Implementation Method of Anti Electromagnetic Interference in Identical and Adjacent Frequency for the Data link of UAV
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The data link, which is the most important part of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), is easily affected by external electromagnetic interference (EMI) in identical and adjacent frequency. To deal with the problem of EMI in frequency band, a method that is early warning and then adopts frequency hopping or other measures is proposed, according to operating frequency band of the data link, the radiation effect experiments on a certain type of UAV's data link under different flight distance are carried out. The experimental results reveal the dynamic range of lost-link thresholds of the data link, on the basis, the suitable EMI monitoring device installed UAV is designed. Several state parameters of the data link such as error rate, receiving auto gain control (AGC) and signal to noise ratio (SNR) are described, and characteristic of the lost-link threshold and the above three parameters in early warning state and lostlink state respectively is compared and analyzed in terms of variety range, 6dB early warning or not, stability of value and correlation with interfering frequency and operating signal power. Finally, a parameter with the lowest uncertainty is determined as the prediction criterion of the data link suffered by EMI, and when external interfering signal power reaches between the early warning value and lost link threshold, the corresponding measures will be activated to protect UAV's data link from interruption.

articleTitle: Wideband High Power Microwave Coupling Analysis of Automotive Engine
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Coupling currents of key wires fixed on an automotive engine were simulated under the consideration of wideband high power microwave (HPM). An electromagnetic model of an automotive engine was built with the consideration of wires connected camshaft and injector separately. Simulation results show that coupling currents are much larger than the working currents of electric devices, and disturbances' frequency characters contain the resonant characters of wires and the spectrum of wideband HPM.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of IGBT Modules in Wind Power Converter Considering the Effects of Different Failure Sites
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: With the extensive investment of wind turbine, it is significant to study the reliability and lifetime estimation model of its core components. Considering the effect of different failure sites on the remaining lifetime, the response of the converter at failure sites is studied. It is found that die attach solder fatigue and DBC (Direct Bonding Copper) solder fatigue, which happen frequently during the serving time, have different effects on thermal loads. A modified Cauer-type thermal model is proposed according to the failure sites. Using a modified lifetime model, Remaining lifetime of the DFIG (Doubly Fed Induction Generator) converter is calculated under different health conditions and failure sites. Reliability analysis is very important to the health management of converter.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Field Uniformity in “Spring-Thunder” Bounded-Wave EMP Simulator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The peak-value distribution of electric fields in testing area in " Spring-Thunder" bounded-wave electromagnetic pulse (EMP) simulator based on parallel finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method on Message Passing Interface (MPI) platform is given. The experiment results are also presented. The field uniformity in "Spring-Thunder" bounded-wave EMP simulator is quantitatively analyzed. The mean value, standard deviation, and the field uniformity of the simulation and the experiment results are got. Both of the field uniformity agree well. It's useful for the selection of the size and the location of the equipment under test (EUT) in the simulator in experiment.

articleTitle: Modeling of a 20 W GaN HEMT Using QPZD Model
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A quasi-physical zone division (QPZD) large signal model for GaN HEMT operating on pulse-mode was established. A 20 W high-power GaN HEMT with power-bar structure, fabricated by in-house 0.4 um AlGaN/GaN HEMT process, is used for validation. All the measured data are fulfilled by an on-wafer load pull measurement system. The results show that good agreements between simulations and measurements have been achieved on pulse I-V, multi-bias S parameters, and large signal performance. The results of this paper show that the QPZD model works well for high power transistors at pulse excitation condition.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Harmonic Suppression of Microstrip Antennas Using Compact Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A single-layer microstrip-fed patch antenna with ultra-wideband harmonic suppression is demonstrated. A compact and novel defected ground structure (DGS) and is introduced. The filtering characteristics of the microstrip patch antenna have been improved. A microstrip antenna with the working frequency 3.13 GHz (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub>) is designed and manufactured. The proposed antenna has an ultra-wide harmonic suppression bandwidth range from 2f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub> to 5f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub>, which is better than the earlier design (2f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub> to 4f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub>). Moreover, the novel DGS decreased the area defected on ground plane by 31.7% compared to the earlier design.

articleTitle: The transmission characteristic of polarized laser in sandstorm on Mars
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper studies the transmission characteristics of polarized laser in sandstorms on Mars. Based on the Monte Carlo simulation method, firstly, polarized laser at wavelength 0.55 micron was selected to calculate and analyze the polarization characteristics of dust particles on Mars at different wind speeds, in different regions and at different altitude. Then, the transmission characteristics of polarized laser at different wavelengths in the environment of dust storms on Mars were calculated and analyzed. The results show that the lower the wind speed, the higher the particle number concentration and the more serious the polarization degradation of Mars dust particles. In addition, the transmission intensity is the largest at wavelength 0.66 micron among the selected wavelengths, and the horizontal decrease and vertical increase at wavelength 7.46 micron are significantly smaller than those of other wavelengths, indicating that the polarization retention at wavelength is better.

articleTitle: A Skeletonization accelerated MLFMA for Volume-Surface Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: To achieve a fast solution of large-scale problems for composite targets, a skeletonization based method for accelerating the MFLMA solution of volume-surface integral equation is proposed. The near-field interactions in the four sub-blocks of the impedance matrix are compressed through skeletonization. To speedup the convergence of the iterative solution, an HSS-based block-diagonal preconditioner is also proposed. Numerical experiments are conducted on a frequency selective surface model to investigate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The implement of the hybrid meshes in US-FETD by using Domain decomposition method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient dual field domain decomposition method is applied to hybrid meshes in the explicit unconditionally stable finite element time domain (US-FETD) to exploit the advantages of the rectangle and triangle meshes. The proposed method implements the hybrid meshes in US-FETD with equivalent electromagnetic current, resulting in a high accuracy of multi-scale electromagnetic modeling. Since the fine structures are inside the subdomain and the US-FETD is used in each subdomain, the proposed method can allow a large time step in whole computational domain. The numerical results can verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Radio Wave Coverage inside Train in Confined Space
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, radio wave coverage properties inside a train located in confined space are studied by using Time-Domain Finite Difference method (FDTD). The works in this paper are mainly focused on the effect of materials of train and windows on the radio wave coverage. Calculation results show that metallic train body will cause a loss about 10 dB. When using Fiber Reinforced Plastic (FRP) as train body, the loss reduces significantly. In addition, for windows, using heat-absorbing glazing leads to an extra loss about 1 dB compared to that of dielectric glass. It is concluded that train material and windows have certain impacts on the radio wave coverage inside the train and need to be further studied.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Aperture-Shared Circular Polarized Array Antenna for X-/Ku-Band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A dual-band aperture-shared circular polarized microstrip array antenna for X-/Ku-band satellite communications is presented in this paper. The antenna is composed of a 4×4 square patch array at Ku-band and a 2×2 cross patch array at X-band. The circular polarization of the antenna is realized by feeding a pair of coaxial lines with 90° phase difference separately. The simulated results of the antenna show that the dual-band impedance bandwidths is 7.1% at Ku-band and 3.6% at X-band and the gains is 16.41 dBi at Ku-band and 13.74 dBi at X-band and the axial ratios are close to the ideal value zero in the operation frequency band. The proposed antenna provides a potential scheme for dual-band satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Multi-Antiparallel Coil for Separation-Insensitive Mutual Inductance Using Ternary-Coding-Based Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Resorting to the superposition principle of mutual inductance, multi-antiparallel coil (MAC) is able to obtain stable mutual inductance as the separation between transmitting and receiving coils changes, which is attractive for range-stable wireless power transfer. This paper presents a new method for the optimal design of MAC. The status of every coil is denoted by a ternary code, and the status code is optimized by a genetic algorithm (GA) to maximize a properly designed fitness function. The global searching ability of GA allows for achieving better design performance than the point matching design method. Besides, with the aid of ternary coding, the GA searching space is limited, and the optimization effort can be reduced.

articleTitle: Efficient TDS-PO Hybrid Method for Scattering Analysis of Large-Scale PEC Target Partially Coated by Thin Dielectric Materials
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In the paper, an iterative hybrid of thin dielectric sheet (TDS) approximation method and physical optics (PO) is introduced for analyzing electromagnetic scattering problems of large-scale PEC target partially coated by thin dielectric materials. The iterative scheme keeps the implementary independence between TDS and PO. Furthermore, the multilevel fast multipole algorithm and the adaptive cross approximation method are adopted to enhance the efficiency for solving the problem in TDS region, and accelerate the computation of interaction between TDS and PO regions, respectively. Some numerical results are exhibited, which elucidates that the TDS-PO hybrid method can efficiently reduce the number of unknowns and the computational complexity. In addition, it also can obtain a better accuracy than PO.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Ultra-thin-Body, DoubleGate pMOSFETs at 5 nm Technology Node
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this work, quantum ballistic transport study of a Si double-gate pMOSFET has been carried out in an ultra-thin structure. The simulation is performed by using non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) solver that incorporates six band k · p model. Based on this framework, we analyze the device characteristics for a channel length of 5 nm considering different transport directions, confinement directions and channel thickness. In the on and off state of the device several physical parameters are necessary for performance analysis including threshold voltage, subthreshold slope, on/off current ratio. Our results confirm that for 5nm gate length, best electrical performance is obtained at (001)/[100] crystal orientation. It is observed that better ON current, subthreshold swing and lower value of tunneling ratio can be achieved by optimizing the channel thicknesses and selecting the proper crystallographic orientation for the device. The I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</sub> /I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</sub> ratio is also calculated for both high performance and low operating power applications. We find that large channel thickness leads to worse sub-threshold slope due to the stronger source-to-drain tunneling caused by electrostatics degradation. The potential barrier and spectral current density are also presented in order to find the source-to-drain tunneling and ratio for different crystal orientations and body thickness.

articleTitle: A Microstrip Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper presents a multilayer 2×2 microstrip circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna array. The simulated impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 13.9%. The 3-dB AR bandwidth is 8.7%. The simulated peak gain of the antenna is 11.7 dBic.

articleTitle: Irregular Subarray Tiling of Small-Scale Wide-Angle Phased-Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, a small-scale wide-angle planar phased-array design based on irregular subarrays is presented. Considering that the control nodes are placed at the subarray level, the increase of scanning angle will generate quantized lobe to form a finite field of view. Increasing the control nodes to reduce the influence of quantization error, the iterative convex relaxation programming is used to achieve the precise aperture coverage and the multitask Bayesian compressive sensing (MT-BCS) solver is adopted to obtain a heuristic initial iteration points to improve the performance of the scanning radiation pattern. Numerical experiments are provided to validate the feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: An Improved Drain-Current Model for FinFETs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, an improved charge-based drain-current model for FinFETs is proposed. The proposed model takes into account the effect of large dynamic changes in temperature. Based on the classic Poisson's equation, an exact charge density expression is proposed by using the Lambert W function. Compared with previous studies, more temperature-dependent terms in the expression of charge density are considered, which can characterize the change in charge density from normal temperature to low temperature. To validate the model, a 4-Fin FinFET with 16-finger in 14nm process is fabricated and the drain-current data was measured over a range of temperatures (84K-295K). Comparing the calculation results with the measured data, the maximum RMS error of drain-current characters has reduced from 0.2623mA to 0.0301mA.

articleTitle: Computationally Efficient Modeling of Time Domain Field-to-Wire Coupling in Multi-Layered Shielded Cables Using JEMS-FDTD
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A computationally efficient time domain field-to-wire coupling model for multi-layered shielded cables has been proposed and integrated into the massively parallel computer code JEMS-FDTD. In this method, multi-layered shielded cables are represented by several transmission line models, each of which is evaluated by solving the multiconductor transmission line equations with the 1D FDTD method. Transfer impedances are utilized to connect the inner and outer transmission line models. The accuracy of the method is validated by simulating the induced currents of a multi-layered shielded cable above a PEC ground plane illuminated by a plane wave and comparing the results with those calculated by using the commercial software. This method has the advantage of simulating the multi-layered shielded cables inside electrically-large objects with high efficiency.

articleTitle: Measurement of OFDM Signals with PAPR Reduction in the Presence of Hardware Impairments
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) has been selected as a 5G New Radio (NR) waveform for carrier frequency below 40 GHz. In order to satisfy the low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) requirement for high power amplifier (PA) efficiency, OFDM with PAPR reduction is highly desirable. In this paper, we evaluate the performance of OFDM with various receiver agnostic PAPR reduction techniques in the presence of hardware impairments. The evaluations are performed in hardware-in-the-loop trials. The measurement results showed that in case of nonlinear PA and high power transmission, OFDM with PAPR reduction schemes can effectively reduce the PAPR of OFDM signals and can achieve similar performance as compared to DFT-spread-OFDM, thus OFDM with simple PAPR reduction is a viable option for 5G NR waveform.

articleTitle: A Circularly-Polarized Frequency-Reconfigurable Antenna with Self-Complementary Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A circular polarized frequency reconfigurable antenna with self-complementary metasurface is proposed in this paper. A novel θ shaped self-complementary metasurface has been proposed and is attached to the substrate to realize frequency reconfiguration. By rotating the unit cell of the metasurface, the resonant frequency of the proposed antenna can be tuned from 37.0 GHz to 41.0 GHz. And the proposed antenna has realized the circular polarization near the resonant frequency. The proposed antenna has good performance in 5G New Radio spectrum.

articleTitle: Conformal spherical array pattern synthesis based on CMA-ES Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient optimization algorithm based on the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy(CMA-ES), is proposed for the synthesis of conformal spherical arrays. The isolated element pattern defined in the local coordinate system is transformed to the global coordinate system by Euler rotation. The pattern of the array can be obtained applying the superposition principle. The excitation weight is optimized by CMA-ES to meet the requirements of low sidelobe pattern. Numerical experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Broadband Circular Polarization Antenna Applied For Base-Station
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper studies the broadband circularly polarized antenna used in micro base stations. The antenna consists of a pair of rectangular loops. The ring patch is used to form circular polarization, and a pair of open resonant ring parasitic elements are loaded between the two rectangular rings to increase the bandwidth. By introducing balun feed to increase bandwidth, good impedance matching can be obtained. Add a metal reflector at the bottom of the antenna to form directional radiation. The antenna was printed on the Rogers RO4003 substrate, and the results showed that the -10dB return loss bandwidth was 43.4% (1.86-2.89GHz), and the -3dB axial ratio bandwidth was 41% (1.9-3GHz). The gain of the antenna in the frequency band is greater than 9dBi.

articleTitle: Antenna Modeling by Nested Kriging with Automated Domain Thickness Determination
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Fast surrogate models may alleviate the difficulties pertinent to high computational cost of electromagnetic (EM)-driven design procedures. Approximation surrogates are by far the most popular but their applicability to antenna modeling is severely limited by the curse of dimensionality. Domain confinement, as in the recently proposed nested kriging approach, offers a viable workaround this issue, in particular, enables the construction of reliable surrogates over wide ranges of antenna operating conditions and geometry parameters. Unfortunately, the original nested kriging method requires the user to set up the domain thickness (the ratio of its lateral to tangential size). The value of this parameter is critical for achieving a proper balance between the model predictive power and the cost of training data acquisition. This paper proposes a procedure for automated a priori determination of the domain thickness and highlights the computational benefits associated with the employment of the presented approach using a dual-band dipole antenna example.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of corporate-feed waveguide slot array antennas by hybrid method of moments and finite element methods
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper presents analysis and design of corporate-feed waveguide slot array antennas by hybrid method of moments and finite element methods. Waveguide slot array antennas realize low loss, high efficiency and high gain simultaneously. The drawback for high speed wireless communication is bandwidth. To enhance the bandwidth, fact analysis method based on method of moments are developed and 16×16-element waveguide slot array is designed. The designed antennas realized 20.4% bandwidth.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Modeling of CMOS Fully Integrated 2.58 THz Thermal Detector
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) detectors have shown attractive prospects in the areas of THz sensing and imaging. This paper presents the multi-physics modeling of an on-chip octagonal ring antenna loaded with a polysilicon resistor coupled with a sensitive proportional to absolute temperature (PTAT) sensor using a 55 nm CMOS process, leading to an uncooled monolithic resonant CMOS fully integrated THz thermal detector. The theoretical analysis, multi-physics modeling, and experimental verification of the detector are presented in detail. The maximum responsivity is 38.04 V/W with a noise equivalent power (NEP) of 2.89 μW/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup> at 2.58 THz for the THz source and an existing atmospheric window, and it has the natural scalability to focal plane arrays, showing great potentials for uncooled, compact, low-cost, easy- integration, and mass-production THz detection systems.

articleTitle: Wave Propagation Modeling in Curved Tunnels with Three-Dimensional ADI-PE Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The alternating direction implicit (ADI) method can be used as an efficient tool to solve the parabolic equation (PE) for wave propagation problems. For curved tunnels, a large number of CPU time and memory are needed because of its large steps and complex direction. In this paper, the bending factor is introduced to describe the curved tunnels. As a result, the calculation for wave propagation can be taken plane by plane along the bending direction. The numerical results verify the efficiency and accuracy of 3D ADI-PE method in curved tunnels by modeling the empty curved tunnel and another curved one with obstacles.

articleTitle: Investigation on Electromagnetic Scattering from Dynamic Sea Surfaces Covered by Natural Sea Slicks
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A model of dynamic nonlinear sea surfaces damped by natural sea slicks is presented. Lombardini et al. model is adopted for predicting the hydrodynamic damping of sea surfaces in the presence of natural sea slicks, and "choppy wave model" (CWM) nonlinear sea surface is utilized for describing the nonlinear interactions between ocean waves. On this basis, the influence of sea slicks' damping on Doppler spectrum of backscattered echoes from contaminated sea surface is investigated by comparison with that from clean sea surfaces. Numerical simulation shows a narrowing of the Doppler spectrum of contaminated sea surfaces compared to that of clean sea. In addition, it is also indicated that the Doppler shift in slicks can decrease or increase, depending on incidence angles.

articleTitle: Research on the damage mechanism of typical radio fuze induced by narrow band HPM
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In order to systematically analysis the damage mechanism of typical radio fuze caused by narrow band high power microwave (NB-HPM), we developed an standard experiment system. Through several rounds fuze experiments form L band to X band, the threshold value, sensitive parameters and main energy coupled channel are defined. By full wave simulation and coupling testing at key points, the key sensitive components is identified. Finally, the damage mechanism is explained by the multiple physical field simulation. All the above work shows that unlike the ultra-band HPM, cannonball body is not the main coupling channel and the silicon controlled rectifier (SCR) would not miss-working by the voltage fluctuation of the commonality ground. Antenna is the main coupling path of typical radio fuze for narrow band HPM from L band to X band. Oscillation tube of RF circuit is the key vulnerable part. The main damage mechanism is heat accumulation in p-n junction and the main effects is miss-fire of fuze.

articleTitle: Investigation of Mutual Coupling Reduction in Base Station Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Mutual couplings in base station array antennas have aroused a great deal of attentions. In this paper, the several decoupling methods are applied to broadband cross-dipole antenna arrays and the corresponding performances are analyzed. It is shown that, for fixed element separation, cross-dipole arrays with compact elements and low profile tend to have good isolation.

articleTitle: An Efficient Way to Calculate the Uncertainty of HEMP Field-Line-Coupling with Nonlinear Load
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The High-altitude Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP) covers a wide range and may damage the electronics and electrical devices. Lots of variables such as different incidence angles could cause the uncertainty in HEMP Field-Line-Coupling. The transmission line always ends with nonlinear loads like MOV, which is far different from the description in HEMP conducting environment standard. In this paper, we are able to give the conducting waveform with any confidence level efficiently by combining Volterra integral equation and Agrawal scattering voltage model based on Polynomial Chaos.

articleTitle: Design of Multifunction Antennas in A Common-Aperture
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A common-aperture antenna that can work in the S-band and UHF band is proposed in this paper. The antenna that works in the S-band consists of a circular patch, a square slot, and a square support post. It is fed by two coaxial cables to achieve circular polarization. Slot antennas that operate in the UHF band are coplanar waveguide excitation. Two pieces of inverted L-shaped patches were implanted into the square grooves to achieve dual circular polarization characteristics. The feeder is terminated on an inverted L-shaped patch. In addition, two rectangular slots were added at the corners of the antenna to improve the bandwidth of the axial ratio (AR) and voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR). Simulation results show that when working in the S-band, the frequency range of VSWR <; 2.8 is 1.9GHz-2.5GHz, and the gain is about 8dB. When working in the UHF band, the frequency range of VSWR <; 3 is 0.66GHz -1.10GHz, and the gain is about 5dB. This antenna has the characteristics of small size, light weight and high isolation.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of an Antenna-Coupled Image-Reject High-Temperature Superconducting Terahertz Receiver
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper presents systematical design, modeling and simulation of an antenna-coupled image-reject high-temperature superconducting (HTS) receiver for terahertz (THz) wireless communication applications. The receiver features an innovative quasi-optical quadrature RF hybrid design comprised of a meta-surface based circular polarizer and a dual-polarized integrated lens antenna fed by two HTS Josephson junctions. Besides, a fully monolithic HTS receiver circuit including on-chip bias tees and quadrature IF hybrid networks, is designed for combining the frequency down-converted signals from the junctions. Detailed numerical modelling and simulations are carried out for optimizing the electromagnetic designs as well as verifying the concept and performance of our presented image-reject HTS THz receiver. The receiver will find huge potential in THz wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Submarine Target Detection Based on Static Electrical Impedance Tomography
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Electrical impedance tomography is a non-invasive, safe, portable imaging technique that enables images of electrical impedance to be reconstructed from voltages measured with an array of electrodes placed on the boundary. Typically, an image data set is collected as a series of many impedance measurements designed to sample as much of the volume as possible. The method, as a typical method for geological studies, is applied for submarine target detection. A method based on complete electrode model and singular-value-decomposition method is applied to reconstruct the conductivity distribution of the DOI. Some numerical results are presented with detailed discussions.

articleTitle: Simulation of EM Scattering from Nonlinear Sinusoidal Sea Waves Modulated by Hydrodynamic Effect in Nearshore Region
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The analysis of the electromagnetic scattering from the nonlinear waves modulated by hydrodynamic effect in nearshore region was presented. The analytical second-order small slope approximation (SSA-2) was applied to investigating the scattering features of the simulated waves which are more realistic than the traditional nearshore waves with constant water depth. The numerical results showed more higher-order harmonic wave scattering features that traditional waves did not presented. The study will be helpful to further probe the nearshore waves scattering.

articleTitle: Study of A RPIM Method Independent of Shape Parameters
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Generally, the value of a shape parameter will affect the accuracy of the radial point interpolation method (RPIM). However, a small shape parameter will cause this meshless method become unstable. In this paper, we expand the Gaussian basis function with a polynomial. Therefore, the calculation based on Gaussian is converted into the calculation of the corresponding feature vector, thereby eliminating the influence of the shape parameters on the performance of the algorithm. The numerical experiments prove the efficiency of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Band Dual-Pattern Radiation Patch Antenna Based on Mode Analysis Theory Under TM01 and TM02 Mode
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A novel dual-band dual-pattern radiation patch antenna is proposed. The structure uses coplanar waveguide feed to realize the design of dual-band dual-pattern radiation. The surface current is analyzed by using the characteristic mode theory, two groups of symmetrical and equal length gaps are loaded in the middle of the patch, and two frequency points are excited to achieve two kinds of radiation pattern. The simulation results show that the design can generate resonance at two frequency points. At 5.16 GHz, TM02 mode is excited, with dual directional radiation, and the peak gain is 1.13 dBi; at 5.48 GHz, TM01 mode is excited, with directional radiation, and the peak gain is 2.81 dBi.

articleTitle: A 3D Printed Plasma Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper presents a plasma Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) with gain and pattern reconfigurability. It consists of a 3D printed DRA and a controllable plasma lump bulb. By changing the excitation state of the plasma, the proposed DRA achieves tunable gain and reconfigurable radiation pattern. The simulated antenna peak gains with turning on and off the plasma are 4.8 dBi and 8.0 dBi respectively. During the reconfiguration, the antenna keeps a wide impedance bandwidth of 51.7% and AR bandwidth of 50.4%. The proposed 3D printed plasma DRA is fabricated and measured for verification. It is low-cost and easy to install, which is suitable for indoor IEEE 802.11b WLAN and other applications.

articleTitle: Electro-thermal Analysis of a 65 nm Channel MOSFET Under The HPEMP
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Thermal effect caused by an external electromagnetic interference seriously threaten to a semiconductor device. In this paper, we have presented an electro-thermal analysis of a 65 nm channel metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) under high power electromagnetic pulses (HPEMPs). The electro-thermal coupled process inside the MOSFET under HPEMPs is numerically studied in this paper by using a 3D TCAD model. The mechanism of heat generation inside the MOSFET is discussed by analyzing the distributions of temperature, electric field and carrier concentration inside the device. The position and structure of the heat source are analyzed. Heat source is a thin layer which lies on the top of the active zone. This analysis is useful for further failure estimating of MOSFET under HPEMP.

articleTitle: VLF Near-field of Radio Wave Penetrating Into A Ground Medium
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In previous studies, the Sommerfeld Integrals (SIs) have been re-examined under the assumption of propagation parameter in air being approximated by γ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> ≈ iλ, in order to derive a few analytical formulas for near-field propagation at specific frequencies (typically below 100 kHz). Here, the resulting formulas are adopted over a plane conducting ground when a vertical magnetic dipole has been chosen as the exciting source for near-field propagation. Computations and discussions are carried out for field components and Poynting energy flow, respectively. Through the analysis, a simple and efficient solution is provided for one to investigate the wave propagation for application of deep underground explorations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Pulse Response Characteristics of AgNWs@SiO2/PVA Composites
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The materials with electrical-field induced nonlinear conductive characteristics for adaptive electromagnetic pulse (EMP) protection are strongly desired. In this paper, the core-shell hybrid nanoparticles of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-decorated silver nanowire hybrids (AgNWs@SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) were synthesized via a sol-gel process employed in a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix material to prepare composites. The characterizations test indicates that the AgNWs were coated with silica and the hybrid particles were dispersed uniformly in matrix. The EMP response characteristics of samples with different filling concentrations under the square-wave were obtained. The results show that the voltage amplitude of output waveform is attenuated obviously, and a reflected waveform appears, which indicates that the resistivity of the sample decreases sharply induced by strong EMP. The mechanism of the EMP response characteristic of the composites was discussed, which verified the application prospects in the fields of adaptive EMP protection.

articleTitle: Differential Evolution Optimization Algorithm for Electromagnetic Device Design with High-dimensional Mixed Discrete-Continuous Variables
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Optimization of electromagnetic device design with mixed discrete and continuous variables is a challenge, especially for those with high-dimensional discrete variables. An orthogonal adaptive discrete variable selection based differential evolution (OADVSDE) is proposed to solve such problems in this paper. Continuous variables use the canonical differential evolution algorithm to perform the genetic operations, while the discrete variables are processed mainly in two steps. The first step is conducted by using orthogonal experimental design to sample a small number of representative combinations. Then good combinations are given more chances to generate more promising offspring in the following generations. To verify its effectiveness, this algorithm is first tested on multi-objective benchmark suites. A design problem of five layers stacked dielectric resonator antenna which involves eight discrete variables with seven possible values for each discrete variable, is also considered. The relevant results show that OADVSDE is superior to the compared algorithm. It can be found that the proposed method is feasible for solving optimization problems with high-dimensional mixed discrete and continuous variables.

articleTitle: Low-Memory Hybrid Discontinuous Galerkin Time Domain Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, a low memory scheme has been proposed to reduce the memory usage of the hybrid method composed of the Helmholtz wave equation based discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method and Maxwell's equation based DGTD method. The hierarchical vector basis functions used to expand the unknowns are expressed in terms of the barycentric coordinate, and the matrices of the hybrid method are decomposed into some unified matrices defined in the local coordinates. With the proposed method, about 18 times memory reduction can be achieved when the full 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order basis functions are employed.

articleTitle: Prediction Scheme of Field Strength Distribution of Vehicle Electromagnetic Immunity Test Based on GB 34660-2017 Standard
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The electromagnetic immunity test of vehicle aims to investigate the working condition of vehicle under electromagnetic interference. With the increasing complexity of road electromagnetic environment, more and more attention is paid to the electromagnetic immunity performance of vehicle. The electromagnetic immunity performance of vehicle is listed as mandatory requirement index by Chinese national standard GB 34660-2017 for the first time. In the stage of vehicle development and design, effective prediction of electric field intensity distribution in the vehicle is helpful to improve the vehicle electromagnetic immunity performance. This paper introduces the requirement of vehicle electromagnetic immunity test in GB 34660-2017 standard and the prediction scheme of field strength distribution in vehicle electromagnetic immunity test is designed, the forward power required by the field strength calibration for simulation and test are compared, and the field strength distribution without vehicle obtained from the simulation and test are analyzed. The results show that the simulation prediction can reflect the actual test to a certain extent. This scheme provides a powerful help for improving the electromagnetic immunity performance in the process of vehicle development.

articleTitle: Simulation of Third-order Inorganic Intermodulation on a Rough Contact Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, the mechanism of passive intermodulation on the metal contact surface is analyzed. According to the roughness contact model, the corresponding equivalent circuit model is established. The influence of metal contact surface roughness, contact area, mechanical loading, and excitation electromagnetic field strength on passive intermodulation power is studied with numerical simulation using ADS. The suppression measures to reduce passive intermodulation products in engineering applications are proposed.

articleTitle: Antenna Topology Optimization Based on Angle-modulated Bat Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper proposes an angle-modulated bat algorithm (AMBA) for antenna topology optimization. Angle-modulated bat algorithm provides a technique that enables the bat algorithm (BA) developed for continuous problems to operate in binary spaces, which has very fast optimization speed and better search performance. Design results of a compact dual-band monopole antenna are presented, showing that the proposed method outperforms the commonly used binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) and binary bat algorithm (BBA) in optimization of time.

articleTitle: An Oscillatory Quadrature Method for the Time-Domain Integral Equation using Laguerre Functions
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The marching-on-in-degree (MOD) scheme which adopts the Laguerre functions as temporal basis functions, is one of the solutions of the time-domain integral equations (TDIE). It has been proved that the oscillatory integrals involving Laguerre functions may cause instability in the MOD method when marching on to a high degree. Therefore, a novel oscillatory quadrature method for Laguerre functions is proposed for stabilizing TDIE-MOD in this paper. The proposed oscillatory quadrature is applicable to the solution of time-domain magnetic field integral equations. Some numerical results of the transient scattering problem are given to show the effectiveness of the proposed oscillatory quadrature for the Laguerre functions in stable solution of TDIE.

articleTitle: Channel shared information encoding with wavelength multiplexed metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Multi-channel information encryption technology has been implemented by metasurfaces owing to their superior capability in manipulating phase, amplitude, wavelength and polarization of incident light. However, any non-full-channel decoding may lead to the leakage of secret information. To further improve the security of information, in this paper, we propose a channel shared information encoding scheme by integrating visual secret sharing scheme with metasurface-based phase-encoding technique. The secret information can be reconstructed only by decoding all the wavelength channels of the metasurface, whiles meaningless images would be extracted in other channel decoding processes, without revealing any original information. The simulated results show the feasibility and adjustability of our encryption system, which can be potentially applied in future optical information security systems.

articleTitle: Broadband CPAntenna Based on the Complementary Circular Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, a new method to design compact wideband circularly polarized antenna based on a complementary circular structure is proposed, and the design rule is explored. The complementary circular structure consists of a 3/4 ring patch and a nearly 1/4 arched slot etched on a ground plane. The ring patch and the arched slot will generate horizontally and vertically polarized electric field E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</sub> and E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sub>, respectively. When the radius ratio of the ring patch to arched slot is close to 0.8, the antenna can operate in a wide band. To validate the idea, an antenna operating in the 5.5GHz is designed. Measured results indicate the realized antenna can operate from 4.8 to 6.5 GHz which agrees with the simulated one. Finally, design method is further tested by two antennas operating in other bands.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization design of a multilayer radar absorbing material
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, the multi-objective optimization design of a multilayer radar absorbing material (MRAM) is demonstrated. Firstly, the MRAM's fast calculation algorithm is proposed and validated to be in a good agreement with the commercial electromagnetic computing software. Secondly, by combining the MRAM's fast calculation algorithm and the NSGA-2 algorithm, a thin, lightweight and fine absorbing performance MRAM is optimized.

articleTitle: Massively Parallel Fully Coupled Simulation of Semiconductor Device Based on Newton-Krylov Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper presents the study of massively parallel fully coupled simulation of semiconductor device based on Newton method. The coupled system is comprised of Poisson equation for the electric potential, and two continuous equations using the constitutive relationship of the drift-diffusion model for the electron and hole concentration. The governing PDEs are discretized in space by a vertex control volume Finite volume method, and integrated in time by the backward Euler implicit method. Solution of the system is obtained by a fully-coupled Newton nonlinear solver, which a BCGSTAB Krylov linear solver with the Additive Schwarz domain decomposition preconditioner is used in each Newton iteration. The program is developed based on JASMIN-platform, named JEMS-CDS-Device. The parallel test results are presented for solution of up to 14 million grid cells scale problem on 16,384 processor of a computer cluster.

articleTitle: Spectral properties of three-slit-box-cavity structured surface simulated by FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The multiband compatible stealth is greatly desired to the military equipment on the battlefield. A three-slit-box-cavity structured surface deposited with SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> film, on which the nanorods array is placed, is proposed for compatible stealth within infrared band of 3-5um, 8-14um and laser bands of 1.06um, 10.6um. The spectral properties of the structured surface are simulated by FDTD method. The effects of geometry parameters on the spectral properties of the structured surface are discussed. The results reveal that the three-slit-box-cavity structured surface possesses amazing spectral stealth properties in the infrared bands of atmospheric window as well as laser bands. This indicates that the three-slit-box-cavity structured surface can be the good candidate for the multiband compatible stealth.

articleTitle: Circuit Modeling of the Cable Shield Injection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Cable shield injection is a kind of pulsed current injection (PCI) test method defined in MIL-STD-188-125-1/2. In this work, taking shielded coaxial cable as an example, a Spice model integrating the model of pulsed current generator with the model of shield coaxial cables for conducted susceptibilities, is introduced and validated by experiment. Furthermore, by analyzing the role of transfer impedance and admittance, some unessential factors for cable shield injection simulation were removed, and then a simplified model is proposed. Comparing to the complete one, the simplified model keeps almost the same accuracy while the complexity is significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Theory and Simulation of Terahertz Gyrotron Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Gyrotron devices are based on the principle of the relativistic electron cyclotron maser and capable of generating high-power coherent radiation in the millimeter-THz wave range, which are important in imaging, communication, biomedicine. However, traditional particle-in-cell software, simulating the beam-wave interaction of terahertz gyrotron devices, is of huge resource consumption due to massive particles and grid-size dependency of wavelength. Specialized theories need to be developed. In this paper, frequency-domain and time-domain nonlinear theories are introduced. Based on macro-particle assumption and 1-D analytic approximation, the resource consumption is dramatically reduced. The results of two theories coincide with each other. The accuracy of simulation result is demonstrated by comparison with particle-in-cell software. The investigation presented in this paper provides efficient and accurate method to analyze the terahertz gyrotron devices.

articleTitle: Kron-Branin Model of Braided Coaxial Cable Illuminated by Electromagnetic Wave
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper develops an innovative model of shielded coaxial cable illuminated by high power electromagnetic pulse. This Kron-Branin model is a flexible and efficient way of wave-circuit hybrid calculation, which is based on Branin’s transmission line (TL) model and tensorial analysis of network (TAN). The traditional equivalent circuit is transferred into a topology graph consists of basic elements like nodes, branches, meshes, and cords. Electromagnetic and circuit equations can be derived and transferred according to the graph. The graph topology and equivalent transmission line equation of illuminated shielded cable structure is presented in this paper. A good correlation between the analytical calculation of the KB model and commercial simulation software is obtained.

articleTitle: The tunable topological valley states in designer surface plasmon crystals based on liquid crystals
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Valley states, originating from 2D layered materials, have drawn much research attention and inspired enormous intriguing physical phenomenon, such as valley Hall effect, valley projected topological edge states and so on. Since valley has been extended into classical systems, some topological properties were deduced and observed in classical wave systems too. However, exploration of practical applications is still on the way due to fixed structure after fabrication. Therefore, in this work, we introduce a nematic LC into designer surface plasmon (DSP) crystal with valleys existing in its band structures, and change the refractive index of LC with external electric field to move the spectral position of topological valley states. Under the action of changeable refractive index, the bulk valley-selective chiral excitation and backscattering-immune broadband valley- projected edge transport have been numerically demonstrated.

articleTitle: An Efficient Hybrid Method for the Optimization of Antenna Radiation Problems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, the scheme of model-order reduction (MOR) combined with tangential equivalence principle algorithm (T-EPA) is proposed to analyze the radiation problem of antennas in the vicinity of a large PEC plate. A limit number of orthogonal basis vectors can be obtained by performing randomized singular-value decomposition (RSVD) on the interaction matrix between the region of radiator and scatterer with a given truncation error. In this way, the wave input-output relation of the scatterer can be encapsulated into a reduced-order model (ROM) which can be pre-computed and reused when the position of the radiator is changed. Furthermore, discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM) is applied to select interpolations on the scatterer to accelerate the filling of interaction matrices. Finally, the combination with T-EPA can reduce the density of unknowns on the radiator and improve the convergence of integral equations in such multi-scale radiation problems. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A physical Charge-based Model for threshold voltage of p-GaN Gate HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This paper proposes a physics-based analytical model for threshold voltage of p-GaN gate HEMT. Based on the EPFL HEMT model, the electric potential obtained by the Poisson's equations is combined with the discontinuity of the interface displacement vector to get the analytical threshold voltage model, considering the total negative polarization induced charge density at the p-GaN/AlGaN interface and the Mg out-diffusion of the p-GaN gate layer. Additionally, the resulting threshold voltage transients are explained using technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations, and good results verify the correctness of our derivation.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Triple-band Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Multi-band antenna and dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) have been playing an important role in the antenna field. In this paper, a triple-band DRA using microstrip line feeding is proposed. The proposed antenna is mainly composed of two cut cylindrical dielectric resonator and FR-4 substrate. By reasonably distributing the position and length of the microstrip feeding line, the antenna proposed in this paper can work in three working bands successfully. Three operating bands with the central frequencies of 6.52 GHz (6.11−6.72 GHz), 7.91 GHz (7.68−8.27 GHz), and 9.54 GHz (9.04−9.72 GHz) have been achieved, respectively. Simulation results show that the antenna also has a good performance in gain and it can be very useful in WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Study on Optical-Electric-Thermal Performance of the Perovskite Solar Cells Based on Embedding Different Geometric Metal Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: When we geometrically optimize the metal nanoparticles embedded in the active layer of perovskite, the light absorption capacity of perovskite solar cells has been significantly enhanced. At the same time, we investigate the effect of metal nanoparticles heating on the electrical performance and stability of perovskite solar cells. The research results show that the heat loss of the metal nanoparticles can be effectively reduced by optimizing the geometric parameters of the metal nanoparticles. The temperature of the perovskite active layer is also reduced. The results show that the carrier mobility of the perovskite solar cell increased. The energy conversion efficiency of the perovskite solar cell increased by 38%.

articleTitle: Investigation and Design of Laser Diode based Diver-to-Diver Optical Communication System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Divers need proper communication techniques as sound waves cannot propagate through water. Research fraternity has designed several underwater communication systems to overcome this intriguing factor of communication. Researchers have opted several approaches for audio signal communication through water. Designed communication systems vary in complex circuitry, audio signal quality, system components and cost. In this present study, we seek to experimentally demonstrate the feasibility of laser diodes and solar cell receiver for audio signal transmission through water. Audio signals were transmitted through water by imposing over blue, green and red LDs. We have examined light scattering and our findings validate laser diode with shorter wavelength gives less scattering. This paper also outlines an approach for out-of-sight communication. In our experimental trials, the maximum propagation distance is 62 cm by using 450 nm blue laser diode. This study also includes discussion of collimating lens effect on audio signal transmission.

articleTitle: Non-intrusive reduced-order modeling of parameterized electromagnetic scattering problems using cubic spline interpolation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: We report a non-intrusive method for the solution of parameterized electromagnetic scattering problems, which requires a database including the time history of the full-order solutions (snapshots) for different parameters. The snapshot vectors are produced by a high order discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) solver. A two-step proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method is employed to extract the time-and parameter-independent POD basis functions. A cubic spline interpolation-based (CSI) approach is introduced to approximate the dominating time- and parametermodes of the reduced coefficient matrices without resorting to Galerkin projection. Then they can be used directly for new time and parameter values to recover the reduced-order solutions during the online stage. Numerical experiments for the scattering of a plane wave by a 2-D dielectric cylinder and a multi-layer heterogeneous medium nicely illustrate the performance of the proposed POD-CSI method.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulations of Roughness Scale Effects on Bistatic Ocean Scattering
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: The effects of roughness scale on bistatic radar scattering from an ocean surface at L-band are studied using the second order small slope approximation (SSA-II) and the method of moments (MoM). Ocean roughness is represented and varied using different ranges of the KHCC03 spectrum. The criteria of full spectrum truncation are also given. Numerical results are illustrated in fully bistatic configuration at 1.26 GHz. Simulations indicate that short waves with wavenumber larger than 316 rad/m (around 12 wavenumbers of L-band incidence wave) have little effect on ocean scattering. The large-scale waves put more impacts on scattering in the forward directions, especially for large incidence angles. The effects of large-scale roughness on ocean scattering are in general smaller at VV-pol than HH-pol. The bistatic scattering at cross polarizations is less sensitive to the roughness scale as compared to the co-polarizations. For numerical simulations of ocean scattering with incidence angle less than 60°, using small surface profiles with size about 1/6 of those accounting for full spectrum yields results of bistatic scattering coefficients with errors less than 2dB.

articleTitle: Scattering study of a time-continuous breaking wave model generated in DualSPHysics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Breaking wave modeling is one of the most important difficulties in the simulation of sea scattering. To explore the scattering characteristics of a more realistic model, a time-continuous breaking wave model is developed in this paper, which is based on the open-sourced package of DualSPHysics. The electromagnetic (EM) scattering of several representative frames is calculated by the two-dimensional method of moments (MoM). In this paper, the characteristics of horizontal polarization (HH) and vertical polarization (VV) scattering under different sea conditions are elucidated. Sea spikes are pinpointed when incidence illuminating at large incidence angles. It turns out that when the wave surges, the scattering of both polarizations at large incident angles increase greatly, accompanied by significant changes in the scattering characteristics, resulting in remarkable sea spikes.

articleTitle: Compact UWB MIMO antenna with quasi-self-complementary half-slot structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A compact UWB MIMO antenna using quasi-self-complementary half-slot structure is proposed in this paper. The quasi-self-complementary half-slot structure consists of a semiellipse radiator and a quasi-ellipse shaped protuberant ground plane, which is the basic element to design the proposed antenna. The application of the quasi-self-complementary half-slot structure provides miniaturization, ultrawideband phenomena and good isolation. The proposed UWB MIMO antenna has compact size of 22.8 × 18 mm, operates from 2.88 to 11.87 GHz, and obtains inherently a good isolation greater than 15 dB.

articleTitle: Investigation on High Power THz Radial Extended Interaction Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: A THz radial extended interaction oscillator based on radial multigap resonant cavity is proposed. The device consists a nine-gap radial cavity as the high frequency structure, which is proposed and optimized around the frequency of 0.14 THz. To drive the nine-gap radial cavity, a divergent radial sheet electron beam with angle of 10 deg and current of 4 A is adopted. A radial solenoid magnetic field of 0.5 T, produced by properly designed coils, is employed to focus such an electron beam. The particle-in-cell method is used to find out the performance of the device. A peak output power of 7.2 kW is obtained at the frequency of 0.146 THz, when the operation voltage is set to 18 kV, the electron efficiency is about 10%.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis of Optical Waveguide using a Novel Symplectic Compact FDTD Schemes
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: For modal analysis of longitudinally invariant optical devices, the compact-finite-difference time-domain is an efficient algorithm for alleviating the large amount of storage space and computing time under the 3D complex structure simulation. However, this algorithm needs to scale down the time step to mitigate the numerical dispersion errors while simulating optical waveguide working at high frequency. Here, a novel high-order symplectic compact FDTD scheme is proposed, which is attributed to the theory combination of the fast-spatial scheme and stable temporal scheme. The research results not only verify the effectiveness by numerical experiment on a planar dielectric waveguide with complex cross section, but also provide efficient theoretical guidance for the design and optimization of optical devices at the nanometer scale.

articleTitle: Research and Design on Low Reflectivity of One-dimensional Metal-Dielectric Photonic Crystal Shielding Film
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In order to improve the visible light transmittance of the one-dimensional metal dielectric photonic crystal shielding film, the optical interlayer anti-reflection design is adopted for the OMPC film system by the equivalent needle layer insertion method. An optical antireflection OMPC composite film system is formed by a composite structure model composed of an optical functional film and an OMPC film system, which increases the visible light transmission ability of the shielding film. The optical interference scattering theory and equivalent refractive index were used to analyze the film structure of the OMPC shielding film, and the refractive index matching method and software-aided design were used to calculate the light transmittance and reflectance of the film system. The result was that the composite film system was significantly improved the transmittance.

articleTitle: Electro-Thermal analysis of SiGe HBT under HPM Injection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, the failure of SiGe HBT is analyzed under high power microwave pulses. The transient simulation is conducted to obtain the temperature distributions and change of junction temperature with pulse injected. The calculated failure results are compared with measurement results which show close agreements.

articleTitle: An active detection approach for hidden radio-frequency receivers discovery
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: This work explores the possibility of identifying the hidden presence of a radio frequency illegal receiver using an active detection approach. Such wireless receivers are quite difficult to detect because they only receiving wireless signals and never transmit them. In this letter, we show that even a passive receiver might be able to detect by comparing its radar echoes when it is in power on and off states. Using an FM radio as a demonstration, the radar back-scattering characteristics of the telescopic antenna loaded with LC circuits in the FM band is simulated in the full-wave solver. In addition, time-domain radar echoes for different waveforms are studied to investigate the performance of hidden receiver detection.

articleTitle: Plasmon tuning and electromagnetic field enhancement of Au@Ag nanorod-gold film nanostructure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: In this paper, the finite element method is used to calculate the extinction optical properties and electric field distribution of gold core silver shell nanorod-gold film nanostructures. The volume ratio of silver and the length diameter ratio of core-shell nanorods can be changed by controlling the thickness of silver layer, which can realize the regulation of the longitudinal mode peak position from 600 to 900 nm. The electric field intensity of the core-shell nanorod-gold film structure increases with the increase of the volume ratio of silver. Silver is the plasmon material with the smallest loss in the visible light region, due to its small imaginary part of the dielectric function and lower plasma damping than gold. Therefore, with the increase of the volume ratio of silver, the extinction spectrum intensity of the gold core silver shell nanorod-gold film increases obviously, and the blue shift of the peak position and the narrowing of the full width at half maximum of the wave shape are obvious changes. At the same time, the structure gap confines the light to the deep sub wavelength range, which will produce a hot spot in the gap, which will enhance the electric field.

articleTitle: Passive wireless temperature sensors for harsh environment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Numerical Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Modeling and Optimization (NEMO)
abstract: Temperature is the key parameter of the operating state in the power system. The occurrence of faults of high-voltage transformer, cable joint and other power equipment is often accompanied by abnormal temperature rise.
